contentBlocks.description: If you cannot work due to a physical or mental condition, you may qualify for the SASSA Disability Grant. Learn about the medical evaluation process, eligibility requirements, and how to apply.

contentBlocks.text: Disability Grant Eligibility and Medical Vetting Guide

Individuals who cannot work due to a physical or mental condition can qualify for SASSA's Disability Grant of R2,400 per month. Unlike the SRD R370, the Disability Grant is a permanent grant designed for long-term support. The application process requires official medical clearance from a SASSA-approved medical officer.

The Disability Grant exists to support South Africans who cannot work due to physical or mental conditions. It provides financial stability for those whose disabilities prevent employment for more than 6 months. The grant is available as either a temporary grant (6-12 months with reassessment) or a permanent grant (with periodic reviews).

David is a 45-year-old former construction worker from Gqeberha. After a workplace accident in 2024, he sustained a spinal injury that left him unable to perform physical labour. His doctor confirmed his disability will prevent employment for more than 6 months. David applied for the SASSA Disability Grant and was approved after completing a medical evaluation. He also explored the Grant-in-Aid as he requires assistance from a family caregiver. This guide covers David's journey and what you need to do in a similar situation.

steps.title: Get a medical referral
steps.description: Visit your clinic or doctor to get a referral for a SASSA medical assessment. Your doctor must confirm your disability prevents employment for 6+ months.

steps.title: Book the SASSA medical exam
steps.description: Book a medical evaluation through the SASSA portal or at your local SASSA office. You will be assigned a SASSA-commissioned medical officer.

steps.title: Attend the medical assessment
steps.description: Attend the examination with the SASSA medical officer. They will assess your condition and complete the official medical report.

steps.title: Submit your application
steps.description: Take the completed medical report, your ID, and supporting documents to your nearest SASSA office to complete the formal application.

steps.title: Wait for processing
steps.description: Applications take up to 3 months to process. If approved, payments are backdated to your application date.

contentBlocks.title: Processing Timeline
contentBlocks.text: Medical assessment booking: 1-2 weeks. Application processing: up to 3 months. If approved, backpay from application date. Reassessment for temporary grants: every 6-12 months.

items: Using a private doctor's report instead of a SASSA-commissioned medical officer — only SASSA-approved doctors count
Submitting a medical report older than 3 months — it will be rejected
Not attending the scheduled medical exam — you must rebook and restart the process
Failing to declare all income sources — SASSA cross-checks with banks and SARS

contentBlocks.text: What to Do If Your Application Is Declined

If your Disability Grant is declined due to 'medical criteria not met', you must file an appeal with the Minister of Social Development within 90 days. Make sure to attach any supplementary medical records, specialist reports, or hospital discharge summaries that support your case. Visit our appeals centre for detailed guidance.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a temporary and permanent disability grant?
faqs.answer: A temporary disability grant is approved for 6 to 12 months when your condition is expected to improve. A permanent grant is for conditions unlikely to change but is still reviewed periodically (every 1-5 years).

faqs.question: Can I receive a disability grant if I get a private pension?
faqs.answer: Only if the private pension income falls below the strict means test threshold of R112,200 per year for a single person.

faqs.question: Can I work while receiving the Disability Grant?
faqs.answer: No. The Disability Grant is for individuals who cannot work due to disability. If you start working, you must report this to SASSA as it may affect your eligibility.

faqs.question: Does the Disability Grant turn into the Older Person Grant at 60?
faqs.answer: Yes, once you turn 60 you will transition from the Disability Grant to the Older Person Grant. The amount is similar, but you must complete a new application.

faqs.question: Can I get both the Disability Grant and Grant-in-Aid?
faqs.answer: Yes. Grant-in-Aid is an additional R580/month on top of your Disability Grant if you require full-time 24-hour care from another person.

faqs.question: What medical conditions qualify for the Disability Grant?
faqs.answer: Any physical or mental condition that prevents you from working for longer than 6 months may qualify. This includes but is not limited to: spinal injuries, severe arthritis, HIV/AIDS complications, mental health conditions, vision/hearing loss, and chronic illnesses.
